name: Your hands
desc: Two hands and a bench of habit. Cutting, stacking, filling, packing: instant, no cells, no energy.
notes: Virtual: not a thing, always owned. Hand recipes are instant, 0 energy, 0 cells.

name: Workbench
desc: A steel bench with a vice, a roller and a rack of hand tools. Repair, refill, bundle, refurbish.

name: Smelter
desc: The old cast-iron furnace, its firebox gutted for a cell rack. Two ore in, one bar out.
notes: Keeps the furnace footprint 3x4 and its ore-in crucible. Composition is iron and firebrick (silicate). Buildable: see rcp_mach_build_smelter.

name: Recycler
desc: A grinding drum and a row of sorting chutes. Anything in, materials out, a tenth to sludge.

name: Crusher
desc: Twin toothed rollers over a steel hopper. Breaks mixed scrap, e-waste and ice into sorted lumps.

name: Purifier
desc: A tall tank with a pump and a filter sleeve. Greywater or melted ice goes in, clean water comes out.

name: Charger
desc: A wall-fed cradle that trickles station power into a spent cell. Billed by the charge, at the power price.

effects.text: Refills a cell for its capacity x the power price, in credits
Charges overnight too; a brownout slows it

notes: Generic rule: any cell in the cradle is refilled; no matter moves. The effects text is the visible price. Buildable: see rcp_mach_build_charger.

name: Hydro tray
desc: A shallow polymer tray with a drip line and a lamp bracket. Seed, water and light turn over nights to crops.

name: Wired terminal
desc: An all-in-one machine with a curved green screen and a floppy drive. It runs on a cell and a wall socket.
notes: Numbers carried from src/kinds.json (memory 640, disk 2048, speed 8).

name: Modem
desc: A beige box with a handset cradle and a line jack. Plugs into the terminal: no modem, no mail.

effects.text: Mail orders reach you: +1 per day (none without a modem)
Lets wholesale and attachment mail through

notes: orders_per_day add is the modem share of the phase rate; task 10 owns the base rate.

name: Slip printer
desc: A thermal slot printer with a roll of paper tape. Order slips, labels and receipts, a strip at a time.

name: Box sealer
desc: A clamp frame with a tape head and a hot wire. Run a packed box through and it comes out sealed.

name: Scanner
desc: A flat bed under a hooded lamp, wired to a sensor head. Shows what a box or a disc is hiding.

effects.text: Security inspection chance -5% while a scanner is powered

name: Radio
desc: A scuffed engineers' set tuned to the maintenance bands. Chatter about breakdowns before they happen.

name: Digester
desc: A sealed iron tun with a stirrer and a vent line. Sludge sours and settles into paste over nights.

name: Vat
desc: A square steel vat with a paddle and a press head. Biomass paste goes in; a disc decides what comes out.

name: Fabricator
desc: A gantry with a feed hopper and a heated bed. A blueprint disc tells it what to make from bar and polymer.

name: Extruder
desc: A heated barrel and a die plate. Polymer flake goes in the top and sheet, tube or film comes out.

name: Kiln
desc: A brick drum on cells with a thick lid. Grit and slag fuse into glass, vials and ceramic.

name: Electrolyser
desc: Twin steel plates in a clear-glass tank, wired to a heavy rectifier. Water splits into gas.

name: Scrubber
desc: A fan box with a slot for an air cartridge. Pulls foul air through carbon; the cartridge does the work.

name: Algae tank
desc: A tall glass tank of green water with a lamp rack and an air stone. Grows biomass and breathes out.

name: Still
desc: A copper pot, a coil and a drip jar. Ferments and distils slowly, and smells of both.

name: Chem bench
desc: A fume-stained steel bench with burettes, a hot ring and a rack of vials. Reagents, solvents, coolant.

name: Pill press
desc: A turret press with a hopper of powder and a tray of dies. A hundred small thumps a minute.

name: Loom
desc: A wide loom rebuilt in light alloy, with a heddle drive. Fibre goes in; cloth and gauze come off.

name: Pulper
desc: A tub with a paddle and a screen. Rags and lint soak into slurry and press out as paper.

name: Galley
desc: A hot plate, a pan well and a fan on cells. No flame, no smoke, and a pot of something warm.

name: Document printer
desc: A flat-bed press with an ink well and a paper tray. Manuals, posters and books, a sheet at a time.

name: Labeller
desc: A hand-fed gummer with a disc-driven print head. Sticks a grade or a licence on whatever you slide through.

name: Disc copier
desc: A twin-drive disc cradle with a bar of green lights. Reads one disc, writes another, and does not ask.
notes: Generic rule: any copyable, unlicensed disc and a blank of the same media become two discs.

name: Chiller
desc: A finned radiator box with a pump and two hoses. Pulls heat out of whatever it stands beside.

effects.text: Overclocked machines beside it drain 5% less

name: Vent port
desc: A hatch on a rail with a bolted collar. Sludge and waste go through for a fee and do not come back.
notes: The outflow port: matter leaves the loop in its recipes (loss) for a credit fee.

name: Hydro rack
desc: Four tiers of trays under strip lamps, with a drip line down one side. Fruit, herbs and fibre crops.

name: Industrial vat
desc: A riveted cauldron the size of a bunk with a screw press. Big batches, gourmet discs, overnight runs.

name: Precision fabricator
desc: A closed cabinet with a granite bed and a probe arm. Tight tolerances: bearings, valves, machine parts.

name: 3D printer
desc: A glass-hooded gantry that lays polymer and light metal in threads. It reads its models off a memory card.

name: Assembler
desc: A cage of jointed arms over a jig. Boards, chips and housings snap together into whole devices.

name: Cell press
desc: A hydraulic press with a clean sleeve. Lithium, metal and reagent are squeezed into charged cells.

name: Synthesiser
desc: A cabinet of reaction coils, cold traps and gas bottles. Builds molecules to order from a card.

name: Cellar
desc: A cold insulated cabinet with a rack of shelves and a slow fan. Cheese and wine improve if you leave them.

name: Jeweller's bench
desc: A fine bench under a loupe lamp, with a micro torch, a jig and a lock-drawer. Noble metal stays here.

name: Annealer
desc: A drum furnace with a quench tank and a timer. Heated and cooled by the book, tools last longer.

name: Banner printer
desc: A wide roller press on legs, with four ink wells and a take-up spool. Banners, art prints, ad sheets.

name: Broadcaster
desc: A rack transmitter with a feed encoder and a disc tray. Pushes your ad onto the deck screens.

effects.text: The advertised need draws 1.5x the walk-ins for a while
+1 walk-in a day while an ad runs

name: Workstation
desc: A tower with a tall green screen, twin drives and a bay of ports. Bigger memory, more devices, scripts.

name: Autofab
desc: A hall-length fabricator with a robot arm, a parts silo and a conveyor. Any blueprint, batches overnight.

name: Bioreactor
desc: A glass-lined tank the height of the deck, with spargers and a sample port. Sludge in, culture food out.

name: Mainframe
desc: A cabinet bank behind a locked cage, humming and warm. Runs every machine on the field and the market clients.

effects.text: Four more machines may run overnight

name: Refinery
desc: A column of crucibles and cold traps, chimney bolted to the hull. Pulls rare earths and noble metal from slag.
